# Add a description field when saving a new prompt (admin) [Jira Issue SCRUM-153]

**Jira Issue:** SCRUM-153
**Title:** Add a description field when saving a new prompt (admin)

**Status:** draft

## Specification

### Goals

###### Problem / opportunity
- Superusers need a lightweight way to document what changed when a prompt is promoted to production.
- Without notes captured at promotion time, later review/auditing and change tracking is harder.
###### Goals
- Require Superusers to enter a short free-form comment describing changes as part of the “promote to prod” flow for prompts (Jira title mentions “admin”; Amir indicated “superusers only” in discussion—confirm final role scope).
- Persist the comment so it can be referenced later (e.g., during review/audit/history lookup).

### Use Cases

![after](data:image/png;base64,)
###### Primary persona
- Superuser (current direction per Amir: “superusers only”; Jira title references “admin”—confirm final role scope).
###### Key use case (JTBD)
- When an authorized user promotes a prompt to production, they must add a brief comment describing what changed, so future reviewers can understand the rationale/delta for the promoted version.
###### Step-by-step scenario
- User initiates “Promote to prod” for a prompt/version.
- User enters notes in a Comments field (required).
- User confirms promotion; the prompt is promoted and the comment is saved with the promotion action/version.

### Solution

![showcase](data:image/png;base64,)
###### Proposed solution
- Add a required text input field during the “promote to prod” save/promotion step to capture a Superuser-provided comment describing what changed.
###### In scope (MVP)
- UI field added to the promote-to-prod workflow.
- Free-form text entry (required to complete promotion).
- Persist the comment on the promoted prompt version.
- Display the saved comment in the prompt version history entry for that promotion.
###### Out of scope (unless later specified)
- Rich text formatting.
- Automated diff generation.
- Approval workflows beyond capturing the comment.
- Editing past promotion comments after the promotion completes (to be decided).

### UX & Requirements

###### UX: Promote-to-prod flow changes
- Add an additional input field on the “promote to prod” screen/modal/step.
- Label: “Comments”.
- Input type: free-form text (single-line vs multi-line TBD).
- Required: yes; user cannot complete promotion with an empty Comments field.
###### Functional requirements
- The system must display a Comments field prior to completing the promote-to-prod action.
- The system must submit/save the comment together with the promote-to-prod action.
- The comment must be associated with the specific prompt version being promoted (so subsequent promotions do not overwrite prior notes).
- After a successful promotion, the saved comment must be viewable in the prompt version history entry for that promotion.
###### Acceptance criteria
- AC1: When a Superuser initiates “promote to prod”, a Comments text field is available before confirming the action.
- AC2: Completing promotion persists the entered comment with the promoted prompt/version.
- AC3: Promotion cannot be completed if the Comments field is left blank.
- AC4: The saved comment is viewable in the prompt version history entry corresponding to the promotion.

### Technical & Risks

###### Data model / persistence considerations
- Add storage for a promotion comment/description.
- Persist the comment on the specific prompt version that is promoted to production.
###### Security / permissions considerations
- Role scope is ambiguous (Jira mentions “admin”, discussion mentions “superusers”); current direction from Amir: “superusers only” (confirm final decision).
- Evidence observed so far:
- Jira issue title: “Add a description field when saving a new prompt (admin)” explicitly references “admin”.
- Jira issue body/description: “when promoting a prompt to prod, add a Comments fields, to allow adding some notes to describe what has changed”.
- Jira issue body/description references “promoting to prod” but does not explicitly name a role.
- In-thread discussion: Amir confirmed “superusers only”.
- Marked/annotated text in the requirement references “Superusers”.
- Ensure only authorized roles can view comments after promotion (visibility rules TBD).
###### Risks / dependencies
- If comments are not displayed anywhere post-promotion, value is limited; requires defined retrieval surface (e.g., history/audit log/version details).
- Naming ambiguity (“Comments” vs “Description”) may impact UI consistency and API naming; requires decision.
- Permission ambiguity (admin vs superuser) can cause inconsistent implementations across UI/API unless decided early.

### Rollout

###### Open questions
- Display surface: resolved — show the saved comment in the prompt version history entry corresponding to the promotion.
- Field label: resolved — use “Comments”.
- Field requirement status: resolved — Comments is required to promote to prod.
- Max length and whether the field is multi-line (tracked in TODO).
- Visibility rules: who can view the comment after promotion?
- Role scope / permissions: PM indicated “Something else — I’ll describe it” (beyond Admin vs Superuser). Define who can promote to prod and enter the required Comments.
- Data attachment point: promotion event vs prompt version vs prompt record.
- Editing rules: immutable after publish vs editable later.

### Open Questions

###### Deferred decision: permissions / role scope
- Decide which roles can **promote prompts to production** and therefore must/are allowed to enter the required **Comments** field.
- Current signals are mixed:
- Jira title references “admin”.
- Prior discussion/annotations reference “superusers only”.
- Status: PM selected “Something else — I’ll describe it” for role scope; awaiting definition.
